s01.translation: Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee, blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus.

s02.translation: Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.

w001.function: Imperative of “aveo” — the ancient greeting: “hail, be well”; the angel's word at Lk 1:28.

w003.function: Ablative: full WITH WHAT — with grace; the received English says “full of grace”.

w004.function: Vocative feminine — the adjective of the address; construes with the ablative “grátia”.

w005.function: Nominative — subject with an understood “est”: the Lord [is] with thee.

w006.function: A fused form: “te” (ablative) + “cum” (with) — with personal pronouns the preposition “cum” follows the pronoun: tecum, nobíscum.

w007.function: Nominative: “blessed [art] thou” — understood “es”. In the Vulgate these words still belong to the angel's greeting (Lk 1:28).

w012.function: Nominative masculine — now of the fruit, not of Mary.

w013.function: Nominative of the 4th declension (fructus, -us) — the corpus's first 4th-declension noun.

w014.function: Genitive: fruit OF WHAT — of the womb.

w016.function: Nominative — apposition to “fructus”: the fruit… Jesus. Dictionary lemma: Iesus.

w017.function: Vocative feminine — opens the petitionary half of the prayer.

w018.function: Vocative — as in the first half.

w020.function: Genitive: Mother OF WHOM — of God.

w021.function: Imperative of “oro” — the same verb as in “Orémus”.

w022.function: Preposition with the ablative: on behalf of — intercession.

w024.function: Ablative plural — apposition to “nobis”: for us, sinners.

w025.function: Adverb of time — the first of the two moments of the petition.

w026.function: Coordinating conjunction — joins “now” to the hour of death.

w027.function: Preposition with the ablative — time: when?

w029.function: Genitive: at the hour OF WHAT.
